where [MATH: N] is the number of eggs produced by the farm during the year, and [MATH: C] is the number of chickens on the farm.

In words, what is the appropriate measurement unit for [MATH: P?]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
We are solving for measurement units, so we can ignore the quantities [MATH: 115] and [MATH: 20\,000.] They do not matter if we are just solving for units.

Since [MATH: N] represents [MATH: \textrm{eggs}] and [MATH: C] represents [MATH: \textrm{chickens},] the appropriate measurement unit for [MATH: P=\dfrac{N}{C}] is [MATH: \dfrac{\textrm{eggs}}{\textrm{chickens}}.] In words, this is "eggs per chicken."
